text:
Nikita Kucherov has 30 points in 21 games, and the headlines around him this month have been as much about his future in Tampa as his play, with Bolavip reporting the Lightning remain reluctant to trade him. Whatever that chatter amounts to, he answered on the ice with a hat trick against Buffalo on Nov. 11.

Our read is mixed. Tampa has scored 7.9 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which pads the assist column. His own shooting, though, is running cold at 12.1%, below the 15.4% we'd expect from him. Those two things pull in opposite directions, and the net is a player producing about what he should.

Evolving-Hockey had him second among all forwards last season at 4.3 wins above replacement, with a large share from even-strength offense, along with a real defensive cost (bottom 11% of forwards in expected goals allowed). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the shape of it: elite setup passing and plenty of shots off royal-road feeds, the pass across the slot that goes in about 25% of the time. Watch the goal total. If the shooting comes back, the points climb.
headline: Kucherov's points are louder than his shot
